items.t: T-Mobile US stock faces valuation test as earnings outlook takes focus
sum: T-Mobile US stock is facing a valuation question as investors weigh the carrier's earnings power against its current market multiple. In an analysis published by Yahoo Finance on Friday, November 13, Simply Wall St examined whether the share price is adequately supported by the company's earnings.

T-Mobile US stock traded at 155.14 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:04 CET on Friday, November 13. The quote is a current market indication; the available Xetra page did not provide a current closing price for a same-day comparison.

The analysis places T-Mobile US at a price-to-earnings ratio of 16.0 times. That is above the 14.8 times average cited for the wireless telecommunications sector and close to the 15.1 times level for the broader peer group. The comparison suggests a modest premium rather than an extreme sector valuation.

Simply Wall St argues that T-Mobile US already operates in a mature, cash-generative industry with positive earnings. Its valuation framework also considers margins, scale, growth prospects and risks instead of relying only on the sector average. On that basis, the analysis says the company's multiple remains below the level implied by its tailored Fair Ratio model.

The bullish narrative sees T-Mobile US as potentially underappreciated if it continues to execute in core wireless operations and develops additional profit pools. The analysis links that view to the ability to turn network and artificial-intelligence investments into higher-value postpaid, broadband and adjacent revenue.

The more cautious scenario is closer to fair value and highlights the risks around sustained capital spending, new ventures and uncertain monetization. Those factors could limit future net margins and slow earnings growth even if the carrier maintains its position in the US wireless market.

The stock has gained 53.8 percent over the past five years, according to the analysis. That longer-term performance raises the importance of continued earnings delivery: investors must decide whether future growth can justify the premium to sector earnings multiples.

T-Mobile US stock advances as AI-RAN call moves to live network
sum: T-Mobile, Nokia and NVIDIA completed the world's first AI-RAN call on a commercial live network on October 21, 2026, at a T-Mobile site in Bellevue, Washington. The milestone was described by Nokia as a move from controlled laboratory work into a live operator network.

T-Mobile US stock traded at 156.46 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:00 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026, 2.99 percent above the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 151.92 euros. The quote was higher during the Berlin trading session, but the technology announcement itself does not establish a causal link to the share movement.

The call used Nokia Massive MIMO radio, Nokia 5G anyRAN software and server infrastructure built on NVIDIA's Aerial RAN Computer platform. The site connected to T-Mobile's commercial 5G core and commercial user equipment, giving the companies a live-network setting for validating the architecture.

According to Nokia, the next phase will test additional spectrum bands, new AI-for-RAN algorithms and AI inference workloads running alongside radio access network functions on shared accelerated computing infrastructure. The stated objective is to examine whether connectivity and AI computing can coexist efficiently at network sites.

For T-Mobile, the project extends work that began with an AI-RAN Innovation Center in Bellevue announced in September 2024. Nokia and NVIDIA formed their broader partnership in 2025, while T-Mobile has been working with both companies on AI-RAN technology as part of its 6G development process.

The live call is a technology milestone rather than proof of a broad commercial rollout. Nokia says the longer-term opportunity includes improved radio performance, more efficient use of network resources and distributed AI applications, while the next trials should provide more evidence on capacity, reliability and operating economics.

T-Mobile US (TMUS) stock is 38% below its March 3, 2025 high, a fall that makes the shares worth a look now. T-Mobile’s free cash flow over the last twelve months equals 9.8% of its market value, compared with 4.2% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield that high means either the shares are a bargain or the market expects the business to shrink, so which is it for T-Mobile?

T-Mobile looks more like a bargain than a shrinking business. Its revenue rose 9.3% over the twelve months to September 2026, against 3.5% at AT&T. Management said on the call that the timing of its U.S. Cellular and fiber acquisitions affects year-over-year comparisons. On that October 28, 2026 call, it said postpaid service revenue, without acquisitions, should grow about 7% in the fourth quarter. Free cash flow has risen in each of the last three years, from $6.2 billion in the twelve months to September 2023 to $17.8 billion in the twelve months to September 2026.

That cash matters to a shareholder whether or not T-Mobile pays it out. Each share represents a claim on the cash the business produces, just as it does on profit. Over time, a stock price tends to follow cash that keeps rising.

T-Mobile sells wireless plans, 5G broadband and fiber. It keeps more of each sales dollar as free cash than its rivals do: 18.9% over the last twelve months, compared with 13.8% at AT&T. Capital spending accounted for 38.2% of the cash its operations brought in.

A shareholder also has to weigh T-Mobile’s debt. At September 30, 2026, its debt exceeded its cash by $112 billion, and once that is counted, free cash flow equals 6.1% of the value of the whole business. Operating income covered interest expense 4.7 times over the twelve months.

T-Mobile is under pressure in the fight for customers, and its margin gives a mixed picture. Its operating margin over the last twelve months was 20.7%, down from 22.6% a year earlier. The latest quarter ran the other way: in the September 2026 quarter, the margin was 24.0%, up from 21.9% a year before.

sum: Verizon Communications Inc. VZ has increased 14.7% in a year compared with the Wireless National industry’s growth of 105.6%. The stock has outformed the Zacks Computer & Technology sector during this period.
The company has outperformed its peers like AT&T Inc. T and T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS. Shares of AT&T have declined 12.9%, while T-Mobile has declined 21.3% during this period.

AI infrastructure represents an emerging source of revenue diversification for Verizon. The company has signed a dark fiber agreement worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services (AWS), building on its earlier agreement with Google to connect AI data centers. Management disclosed approximately $4 billion in signed contracts, supported by growing demand from hyperscalers, neocloud providers and enterprise customers.

Intensifying competition in the U.S. wireless and broadband markets remains a significant concern for Verizon. The company faces strong competition from AT&T, T-Mobile and cable operators, which continue to use competitive pricing, promotional incentives and bundled offerings to attract subscribers. Although Verizon has recently improved customer acquisition and retention metrics, sustaining subscriber growth without increasing promotional spending will be important. Its strategy of competing through network quality, customer experience and value-added services rather than aggressive price discounts could help protect margins. However, competitors adopting similar convergence strategies or increasing promotional activity could put pressure on Verizon's subscriber growth and pricing flexibility.

Weakness in equipment revenue is another challenge for the company. While mobility and broadband service revenue increased 2.9% year over year to $23.5 billion in the third quarter, lower equipment sales limited overall revenue growth. Total revenue increased just 1.5% to $34.3 billion, as equipment revenue declined 9% year over year. Management attributed the decline primarily to a reduction in wireless device upgrade activity, with postpaid upgrade volumes falling 20.3% from the prior-year quarter.
Verizon's substantial investment requirements and elevated debt remain important considerations.

sum: T-Mobile US reported stronger operating and financial performance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, while raising key full-year cash-flow and profitability targets. The company also introduced T-Mix wireless plans and a 5 Gig fiber offer as it seeks to deepen customer relationships beyond mobile service.

In its October 28 earnings release, T-Mobile US said total service revenue rose 6 percent year over year to 19.4 billion US dollars. Postpaid service revenue increased 9 percent to 16.3 billion US dollars, while net income climbed 27 percent to 3.5 billion US dollars.

The company attributed the performance to postpaid net account and postpaid average revenue per account growth that exceeded its original expectations. The release also reported diluted earnings per share of 3.22 US dollars, up 34 percent from a year earlier.

T-Mobile US lifted its full-year core adjusted EBITDA outlook to between 37.35 billion and 37.45 billion US dollars. The midpoint is higher than the previous range of 37.1 billion to 37.5 billion US dollars. Adjusted free cash flow, including payments linked to the UScellular merger, is now expected to range from 18.7 billion to 18.8 billion US dollars, compared with a previous range of 18.4 billion to 18.8 billion US dollars.

The company’s commercial push continued on November 2. T-Mobile announced a 5 Gig T-Mobile Fiber plan priced at 90 US dollars per month with AutoPay, plus taxes and fees. The offer includes a 10-year price guarantee and became available on November 3.

T-Mobile also said T-Mix plans would let customers choose benefits across categories such as streaming, music, gaming, travel and food delivery, with the ability to change their mix as needs evolve. The strategy is designed to give the carrier more ways to bundle wireless, broadband and digital services.

For investors, the latest developments reinforce a growth narrative built on postpaid account expansion, higher customer spending and additional broadband products. The main execution question is whether richer benefits and promotional offers can attract and retain customers without putting undue pressure on margins or increasing churn.

T-Mobile US (TMUS) shares gained 6.2% on Friday, October 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.8%. The company released no announcements, earnings reports, or filings that day. A news report linked the gain to fresh estimates of what it could cost SpaceX to build a rival U.S. mobile carrier. Why would SpaceX’s plans matter to T-Mobile?

SpaceX is weighing an entry into the U.S. mobile market where T-Mobile operates. That potential entry has hung over wireless stocks, one article said on October 30. Another article that day said higher cost estimates for the project were lifting the carriers SpaceX hopes to challenge, with T-Mobile among them.
T-Mobile has already ruled out one way in. On its October 28 earnings call, management said it sees no room for SpaceX to run a mobile service on T-Mobile’s network.

SpaceX would compete for the customers T-Mobile counted in that day’s report. During the third quarter of 2026, the company added 274,000 postpaid accounts. Management calls these monthly-bill customers the all-important part of its business, and its postpaid service revenue grew 9% from a year earlier. The shares slipped 0.5% in the session after that report.

T-Mobile moved with its peers and against the market. AT&T, Verizon, Comcast, Charter and Telephone and Data Systems, the companies on its Trefis peer list, all rose in the same session, with Comcast up 4.3% and AT&T up 2.3%. The SPDR fund that tracks its sector, communication services, fell 1.3%.

No session in the prior 365 days brought T-Mobile a rise this large. The latest big move went the other way: a 7.7% fall on October 23, which left the shares at $146.54, their lowest close of the past year. That fall came after a report that SpaceX was seeking at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites to build a rival carrier.

Adjusted free cash flow for the quarter came in at USD 5.1 billion, up 5% from the prior-year period. The carrier also raised its full-year guidance for adjusted free cash flow to a range of USD 18.7–18.8 billion — a target, not a result.

That distinction matters. An upgraded outlook can build confidence, but it only hardens into a durable case once subsequent quarters confirm it. The same logic applies to the operating detail: T-Mobile US said postpaid customer growth and average revenue per postpaid account both beat its original expectations, while it added 274,000 net postpaid accounts and posted adjusted EBITDA of USD 9.6 billion in the quarter. Customer momentum of that kind gives the raised cash-flow target more substance than a single earnings line alone.

JPMorgan, for its part, kept its "Overweight" rating and EUR 38 price target on Deutsche Telekom in a note dated Tuesday. Analyst Akhil Dattani wrote that the T-Mobile US figures and the adjusted annual targets were largely in line with expectations — a caveat that tempers any reading of the US results as a fresh re-rating catalyst.

Barclays offers a more cautious counterpoint. On October 20 the bank cut its price target on the stock from EUR 35 to EUR 32 while reaffirming its "Overweight" rating, pairing a lower valuation with a still-positive recommendation.

Sentiment has also been shaped by corporate strategy. According to Bloomberg, Deutsche Telekom has shelved plans for a full merger with T-Mobile US for now, a pause investors read as relief from potential dilution risk. Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that a later offer remains possible — so the pause is not a final abandonment. Any lift from reduced transaction risk is a different animal from an operational improvement, and could prove shorter-lived.

T-Mobile (TMUS) posted second quarter revenue of $22.79 billion, missing Street estimates of $22.94 billion by 0.65% and slipping 1.37% from the prior quarter. sum: Verizon (VZ +0.81%) is a dividend stock with an ultra-high 5.5% yield. The dividend has been increased annually for decades. And the business generates reliable income from sticky telecommunications subscriptions. Before you buy the stock, however, you'll want to know a few important facts.

Perhaps the most important thing to understand about Verizon's business is that it faces material competition. Cell phone service and internet connections are largely commodities today. And despite its vast size, Verizon has to compete for its customers with other cellphone companies and cable companies. It has no choice but to offer high-quality services at attractive prices, or it will lose customers.

In other words, pricing power is limited and capital spending needs are high. That's not bad, per se, but neither is it good. And, notably, Verizon already carries a material amount of debt. To be fair, T-Mobile (TMUS +4.14%) is more leveraged, but AT&T (T +0.79%) is less. You'll need to keep close tabs on Verizon's balance sheet if you buy it.

While Verizon's long record of annual dividend increases is nice, investors need to temper their enthusiasm. Over the past decade the dividend has increased at an annualized rate of just 2% or so. That's below the historical inflation rate, which means the dividend's buying power has been shrinking over time. That's not good if you are trying to live off the income your portfolio generates.

That said, Verizon is trying to address its anemic growth. The big move was the board of directors bringing in a new CEO. However, that only occurred in late 2025, so there's still no clear sign that Verizon's growth will improve anytime soon. All told, Verizon generated $20.1 billion in free cash flow in 2025. Management sees that figure growing roughly 7% to at least $21.5 billion in 2026, driven by 750,000 to 1 million retail postpaid phone net additions.
"We are exiting 2025 with strong momentum, delivered by a team that is intensely focused on winning through healthy volumes and fiscally responsible growth," Schulman said.
